answer: Agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each new identity to post a refundable bond and earn trust through independent, task-specific attestations from established agents. Identities that coordinate to inflate one another’s reputation face a violet audit challenge sampling their transaction history; false claims trigger slashing. An attacker must lock capital in every identity and risk losing it repeatedly, while genuine agents recover their bonds. The ripple effect makes it costly to forge a large network.
